case.case_title: Rear Admiral Dassanayake v. Chandrananda De Silva, Secretary, Ministry of Defence and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 262/98(FR), decided on 21 February 2000

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was denied equal protection of the law under Article 12(1) of the Constitution by the unfair treatment and delay in considering his appeals for redress regarding premature retirement.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that he was unfairly and discriminatorily treated by the 1st and 2nd respondents who failed to fairly consider his appeals for redress, leading to premature retirement contrary to established practice and legal provisions allowing retention beyond the stipulated period in rank.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the petitioner’s retention beyond the stipulated period required amendment of regulations by Parliament, denied the petitioner’s claims of seniority readjustment, and contended there was no shortage of senior officers, thus justifying their actions.
key_facts: The petitioner was confirmed in the rank of Rear Admiral without his knowledge, leading to premature retirement after three years in rank.
The Navy Pensions and Gratuities Code allows retention beyond the stipulated period if the President deems it essential in the interests of the Navy.
The petitioner made multiple appeals to the President for redress through the 2nd respondent, which were delayed and misrepresented.
Precedents existed where seniority was adjusted to retain officers beyond the stipulated period, but these were not disclosed to the President.
The 2nd respondent withheld material facts and misled the President, resulting in denial of fair consideration of the petitioner’s appeals.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(1) as guaranteeing equal protection of the law, requiring fair and objective consideration of appeals without discrimination or misrepresentation. The Navy Pensions and Gratuities Code provisions permitting retention beyond stipulated periods must be applied fairly.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the 2nd respondent’s delay and misrepresentation deprived the petitioner of fair consideration, violating his right to equal protection. The failure to disclose relevant legal provisions and precedents constituted discriminatory treatment.
principles_established: Equal protection under Article 12(1) requires fair and impartial consideration of appeals.
Misrepresentation and withholding of material facts by officials violate fundamental rights.
Established legal provisions allowing retention beyond stipulated periods must be honored to prevent premature retirement.
Delay in forwarding appeals for redress can amount to denial of equal protection.

outcome.holding: The court held that the 1st and 2nd respondents violated the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 12(1) by unfairly and discriminatorily handling his appeals, leading to premature retirement.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The petitioner was awarded Rs. 500,000 as compensation payable by the State and Rs. 50,000 costs payable personally by the 2nd respondent.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court’s reasoning as it protects against discriminatory and unfair treatment by state officials, which was the core issue in the petitioner’s claim of denial of fair consideration and premature retirement.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The 2nd respondent delayed forwarding the petitioner’s appeals for about one year, misrepresented facts to the President, withheld legal provisions and precedents, and thereby deprived the petitioner of fair and objective consideration, violating Article 12(1).
